title: Homily LXIII
subtitle: Matthew 19:16
author: chrysostom
excerpt: “And, behold, one came and said unto Him, Good Master, by doing what, shall I inherit eternal…

footnotes.2: 1 Tim. vi. 10. [R.V., “a root of all kinds of evil.”]
footnotes.3: Matt. xix. 17. [This clause is found in the rec. text, but not in the better supported form of the verse, which reads, “Why askest thou me concerning that which is good? One there is who is good.” It is probable, but not certain, that Chrysostom accepted the other form of the text. Comp. note on Homily XXVII. 5., p. 186.—R.]
footnotes.7: [φησν, “one may say,” occurs in the Greek here.—R.]
footnotes.8: Matt. xix. 20. [R.V. omits “from my youth up.”]
footnotes.9: [An important sentence is omitted here: “But that also was not a little thing which he supposed he lacked, nor did he think that what he had said sufficed for attaining what he desired.”—R.]
footnotes.14: Matt. xix. 23. [The citation is a combination of this verse and Mark x. 23. The influence of Mark’s more striking account is seen throughout the Homily.—R.]
footnotes.16: [R.V., with the same Greek text, renders, “to go through a needle’s eye.” The variation in the English above seems unnecessary.—R.]
footnotes.19: Matt. xix. 27–29. [The position of the word “lands” is peculiar; “or wife” is not found here, but occurs in Homily LXIV. 1.—R.]
footnotes.20: [The following clause is omitted in the translation: “though (or, if) as a whole it seems difficult to them.”—R.]
footnotes.21: [The Greek adds here, κα περιβλλεσθαι πλεω, and to possess himself of more.—R.]
